fr.elements: Main Building; Front Driveway; Access Road; Open Green Space; Landscaped Area; Open Terrain; Perimeter Fencing; Street Frontage; Pedestrian Walkways; Detached Structure
fr.considerations: Single Access Point; Long Driveway; Dense Vegetation; Open Terrain; Limited Rear Access
fr.recommendations: Ensuring the single access point and extended driveway remain unobstructed could significantly improve response times and apparatus maneuvering, particularly for larger emergency vehicles. Keeping the driveway clear of parked vehicles and maintaining adequate vertical clearance along the approach would support efficient access to both the main building and detached structure. Clearly marking the primary access point from the street frontage may assist responding units in locating the entry during low-visibility or nighttime conditions. Given the limited rear access, identifying and communicating an interior staging area to local responders in advance could facilitate more effective operations across the property.

wildfire.conditions: Scattered Shrubs; Continuous Grass Cover; Heavy Ground Vegetation; Brush Concentration; Scattered Shrubs; Fuel Continuity; Limited Defensible Space; Vegetation Adjacent to Structure; Open Terrain; Brushland Interface; Single Access Route; Scattered Trees
wildfire.recommendations: Reducing the concentration of brush and managing the continuous grass and heavy ground vegetation in the area surrounding the structure could meaningfully improve defensible space and reduce fuel continuity near the building. Thinning or removing shrubs closest to the structure and creating separation between remaining vegetation and the building perimeter may reduce direct fuel exposure to the structure. Where scattered trees are present near improvements, removing low-hanging limbs and reducing understory vegetation beneath the canopy could help limit vertical fuel continuity. Given that a single access route serves the property, keeping that route clear of encroaching vegetation along its margins would support firefighter access and improve conditions for both suppression operations and evacuation. Maintaining a well-managed buffer of reduced fuel immediately surrounding the structure, and where feasible expanding that buffer outward through the surrounding brushland, could further improve overall wildfire resilience and property preparedness.
